record.paper_title: A short tour of operator learning theory: Convergence rates, statistical limits, and open questions
record.original_question: Which classes of operators arising in scientific applications are both practically relevant and mathematically structured enough to admit algebraic minimax sample-complexity rates for operator learning?

evidence.quote: Another important challenge is to identify classes of operators that are practically relevant in scientific applications, but still enjoy algebraic minimax sample complexity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mathcal{Y}$ be separable Hilbert spaces (for instance, $L^2$ spaces over compact domains in $\mathbb{R}^d$), and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a class of (possibly nonlinear) operators $F:\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{Y}$. Given $n$ i.i.d. input–output pairs $(X_i, Y_i)_{i=1}^n$ where $X_i$ is drawn from a probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathcal{X}$ and $Y_i = F^\star(X_i) + \varepsilon_i$ for some unknown $F^\star\in\mathcal{F}$ and centered noise $\varepsilon_i$, define the minimax risk
$$ R_n(\mathcal{F}) \;=\; \inf_{\widehat{F}_n}\;\sup_{F^\star\in\mathcal{F}}\; \mathbb{E}\,\bigl\|\widehat{F}_n - F^\star\bigr\|_{L^2(\mu;\mathcal{Y})}^2, $$
where the infimum is over all measurable estimators $\widehat{F}_n$ based on the sample.

A class $\mathcal{F}$ is said to admit an algebraic minimax sample-complexity rate if there exist constants $c,C>0$ and an exponent $\alpha>0$ such that
$$ c\, n^{-\alpha} \;\le\; R_n(\mathcal{F}) \;\le\; C\, n^{-\alpha} \qquad \text{for all sufficiently large } n. $$
Many natural function-space classes (e.g.\ general Lipschitz operators between infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces) suffer from infinite-dimensional curse-of-dimensionality phenomena and only admit logarithmic rates in $n$.

Problem. Identify classes $\mathcal{F}$ of operators arising in scientific applications—such as solution operators of parametric partial differential equations, Hamiltonian flow maps, homogenization operators, or parameter-to-observable maps in inverse problems—that are
(i) practically relevant to scientific computing, and
(ii) sufficiently structured (through smoothness, low effective dimension, holomorphic parameter dependence, multiscale structure, etc.) that the minimax risk $R_n(\mathcal{F})$ obeys an algebraic decay $n^{-\alpha}$ with explicit exponent $\alpha>0$ independent of any ambient infinite dimension.

Provide such a class, together with matching upper and lower bounds establishing the algebraic rate.
artifact.status_search_result: This is posed as an open research direction in operator learning theory. Recent works establish algebraic minimax rates for specific structured classes (e.g., linear/Hilbert–Schmidt operators, holomorphic operators with summable Taylor coefficients, Lipschitz operators with low-dimensional latent structure), but a comprehensive identification of practically relevant scientific-computing operator classes admitting algebraic rates remains an active and open research program.
